title: Time to taste what you share
meaning: Sharing the flavour of a small pleasure can satisfy you more than a tempting continuation that leaves no time to feel what you have received.
text: Generous leisure may need a rather quiet continuation. The Empress in the physical position of Svadhisthana helps you arrange a delicious, beautiful activity for two: preparing treats, finding interesting materials and giving the evening a shape. The Devil in energy urges you to hold onto enjoyment through repetition: another portion, another purchase, another round. The Hermit in emotions suggests a different pace, listening to an impression and distinguishing your own pleasure from the surrounding noise. The pull to continue can therefore conflict with a need to understand what you have already received.

For example, you choose unfamiliar teas and arrange a small tasting at home. The first flavour invites discussion, but the next is already waiting on the table. **Pleasure grows deeper when it has enough of your attention.** A few minutes with one cup let you notice a subtle taste, recall a similar scent and hear each other’s impressions. You need not open every packet for that shared discovery.

Things become harder if stopping feels like losing interest. You add new flavours to preserve enthusiasm, while inwardly wanting more quiet. That withdrawal can be mistaken for indifference to the activity. Offering even more then widens the difference in pace. A pleasant pause leaves you room to understand what you enjoyed and meet again in conversation about an impression you actually shared.
